subject: Questions on log/backups retention and proof of erasure

Date: Thu, 7 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Data retention specifics for logs/backups/prompts (DPA/SCCs)

Hi Priya,

MediSys InfoSec is working through our DPA and SCCs review. A few follow-ups from our auditor around retention and proof of deletion:

1) Can you provide the retention windows for operational logs (auth, trace, request/response) and whether request/response logs may contain prompt text or user-supplied content?
2) What is your backup snapshot schedule and how long snapshots are retained (incl. incremental backups)? Are snapshots excluded from prompt retention policies or are they subject to the same TTL?
3) If a customer requests deletion (DPR), what is the end-to-end timeline (queueing, snapshot purge, KV cache) and what evidence do you provide that deleted data has been purged?
4) Do you have SOC 2 evidence or a mechanism for attestations we can include with our DPIA?

We'd appreciate a short, itemized response we can hand to our legal/audit team. If you prefer a quick call, please propose times.

Thanks,
Carl
Security Manager, MediSys
security@medisys.com

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: priya_natarajan@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: FWD: Data retention specifics for logs/backups/prompts (from MediSys)

Priya —

Quick answers (operational state as of today):

- Operational logs:
  - Auth and metadata logs: retained for 180 days by default, indexed for search during that window. Contain no plaintext prompt content; request metadata (IP, user-agent, request IDs) only.
  - Application request/response logs (debug level): by default disabled for hosted customers. If enabled, debug logs that include request/response bodies are retained for 30 days and written to a customer-scoped, access-controlled bucket. We mark this as "customer opt-in debug capture" in the retention matrix.
  - Error/trace logs: retained for 90 days for diagnostics, no prompt content unless debug capture enabled.

- Backups / snapshots:
  - Full snapshot cadence: weekly full snapshots + daily incremental. Snapshots are retained for 90 days by default (configurable on Dedicated/Private). Snapshots do capture persisted model artifacts and state but do not capture ephemeral KV caches or the in-memory prompt cache.
  - Snapshots do not contain live prompt traces unless debug capture was enabled and persisted into storage (see above).

- Deletion/DPR flow:
  - Step 1: Customer request received (ticketing) — ack within 24 hours.
  - Step 2: Data deletion job queued; we delete application-level records from primary stores within 72 hours.
  - Step 3: Snapshot purges: snapshots containing customer data are scheduled for deletion in next snapshot maintenance window. Because snapshots are immutable, TTLs may require up to one snapshot cycle (max 7 days) to fully reflect deletion; full purge from snapshot retention storage completes within 30 days for hosted customers.
  - Step 4: Indexes and search replicas are rebuilt; residuals removed within 30 days.

- Evidence options:
  - We can provide: timestamped deletion log (job id + timestamp), retention_matrix_v1.3.pdf (explains default vs opt-in), and a SOC 2 Type II report link.

Caveats / notes:
- For Dedicated customers we can reduce snapshot retention and coordinate a more aggressive purge schedule as part of contract terms.
- For Private/on-prem, retention is customer-managed; Redwood can provide deletion playbooks and verification scripts.

If you want, I can produce a single-line summary table for each item that you can forward to MediSys.

Marcus
Sr. Infrastructure Engineer

From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Data retention specifics for logs/backups/prompts (DPA/SCCs)

Carl —

Thanks for the patience. Below is a concise, itemized response you can share with legal/audit. I've attached the retention matrix and the snapshot schedule as requested. Where applicable, I included what evidence we can provide.

1) Operational logs (auth, metadata):
   - Retention: 180 days.
   - Contains prompt text: no — transport and auth metadata only.
   - Evidence: retention_matrix_v1.3.pdf + timestamped export of log index ranges on request.

2) Application request/response (potential prompt content):
   - Default behavior: debug capture is disabled for hosted customers (no prompt bodies persisted).
   - If customer opts into debug capture: retained 30 days in a customer-scoped bucket (access-controlled).
   - Evidence: storage access logs + deletion job id and timestamp when requested.

3) Error/trace logs:
   - Retention: 90 days; no prompt content unless debug capture enabled.

4) Backups and snapshots:
   - Cadence: weekly full snapshot + daily incrementals. Default retention: 90 days.
   - Snapshots do not include ephemeral KV caches; they may include persisted artifacts. Snapshots will not include prompt bodies unless debug capture persisted them.
   - Evidence: backup_snapshot_schedule.csv + snapshot deletion audit trail (provided on request).

5) Data deletion / DPR timeline (hosted customers):
   - Ack: within 24 hours.
   - Primary store deletion: within 72 hours after verification.
   - Snapshot purge propagation: can take up to one snapshot cycle (up to 7 days) before a snapshot is eligible for deletion; full removal from snapshot retention storage completes within 30 days.
   - Index and replica cleanup: completed within 30 days.
   - Evidence provided: timestamped deletion job IDs, audit logs, and (when required) a signed attestation referencing the SOC 2 report.

Notes: For Dedicated customers we can accelerate snapshot TTLs contractually; for Private deployments customers control snapshot retention and we provide verification scripts.

Links/evidence: SOC 2 Type II report: https://redwood-inference.s3.amazonaws.com/compliance/SOC2-Type-II-2027.pdf
Retention matrix (attached): retention_matrix_v1.3.pdf
Snapshot schedule (attached): backup_snapshot_schedule.csv
Google Drive folder with supporting exports (read-only link): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB2cRetentionEvidence

If your auditors need a signed attestation, we can provide a short attestation doc referencing deletion job IDs once the DPR is executed. Happy to set a calendar for a walkthrough with Marcus if their team prefers a technical call.

Regards,
Priya
Director, Business & Solutions
Redwood Inference
